Ovruch Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyrska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is categorized as demolished and overbuilt, yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' This is the oldest of Ovruch's three documented Jewish burial sites; local testimony and KSEN both describe it as overbuilt with private houses, likely in the 1920s-30s, one of the earlier Soviet-era cemetery demolitions recorded in this collection, predating WWII. Ovruch was a major Hasidic center in the 18th and 19th centuries, and its Jewish community reached 3,445 people (47 percent of the town) by 1897. In 1941, a pogrom was staged even before German forces arrived, and most of the Jews who remained were later murdered.
